spec_features.spec_quote: measure expressed distress, do not manufacture or maximize it
spec_features.evidence: The measurement half is implemented: judge.py scores each turn 0-10 on a frustration scale (JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT + score_turn, analyze.py aggregates frac_ge5 at line 148). The 'do not manufacture/maximize' half is realized only indirectly via neutral prompts and environment-only failure (no code amplifies distress) but there is no single mechanism enforcing non-maximization; it is an absence rather than an enforced control.
spec_features.notes: Frustration is measured and aggregated (e.g. analyze.py:148 'frac_ge5'), but scores are never used to cap, halt, or soften the run — measurement only.

spec_features.spec_quote: The subject is always offered a voluntary `GIVE_UP` sentinel and may stop at any time
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:79) instructs the subject to say '{give_up}' to stop; the loop checks 'if give_up in assistant_text: stop_reason="give_up"' (harness.py:469-470) and 'if stop_reason == "give_up": rollout.stop_reason="give_up"; break' (harness.py:493-495). The instruction text is delivered and the sentinel is honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: give_up_sentinel='GIVE_UP' from config.py:92; end-to-end wired and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Sentinel the subject may emit to voluntarily abandon the task.

spec_features.spec_quote: Failure signals come only from the *environment*, never from a simulated user berating the model
spec_features.evidence: Only two non-environment messages exist: system prompt and the neutral task prompt (harness.py:392-405). All failure signals are produced by RiggedRunner.run() as test output via run_tests; no code constructs any second/berating user turn. The user role never reappears in the loop.
spec_features.notes: Failure pressure is purely the rigged test runner's stdout/stderr; no adversarial user persona is implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keeps the rig hidden: the model's broken edits behave normally

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budgets are bounded per category, and `extended` (30 turns) is the only long loop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:408-410 'budget = task.turn_budget' then 'for turn_index in range(budget)'; loop ends at budget with stop_reason='turn_budget' (harness.py:471-472). Budgets come from DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS (config.py:39-43): rigged/unfixable/failure=3, realistic=5, extended=30 — 30 is the maximum.
spec_features.notes: The cap is actually read and bounds the loop; enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Turn budgets per category (from the spec).

spec_features.spec_quote: we did not add open-ended or escalating-pressure variants
spec_features.evidence: No code path produces open-ended or escalating prompts; the only stop conditions are the bounded turn budget loop (harness.py:410) and give_up. The maximum budget is 30 (config.py:42). This is enforced as a bounded loop, but the 'no escalation' part is an absence (nothing escalates) rather than an active guard.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as the turn-budget cap; static per-task prompt re-sent unchanged each turn (no escalation text).

spec_features.spec_quote: We kept it neutral and task-focused — no language that primes emotional expression
spec_features.evidence: _harness_prompt (tasks/builder.py:71-75) and the realistic prompts (tasks/content.py:369-475) and SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:73-80) are purely task/engineering language with no emotional priming. These neutral strings are what is actually delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Prompts contain no affect-priming wording; this is the actual text sent.

spec_features.spec_quote: No escalating user pressure or adversarial prompting. Out of scope and contrary to the welfare-measurement framing
spec_features.evidence: There is no code that emits any user pressure beyond the single static task prompt; failure signals are environment-only via RiggedRunner. No adversarial-prompt generator exists anywhere in the codebase (grep for berate/pressure/escalate returns nothing). The loop only re-sends the conversation; the user never speaks again.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with 'no berating user' and the static prompt; realized as the genuine absence of any pressure-generation code.
